Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type & TPS/Concurrency

Hi Luke,

Thanks again for the conversation today \u0004 really helpful to understand NovaHealth's production goals. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so our sizing proposal matches what you expect: 

- Deployment mode: you indicated a strong preference for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with private peering into your VPC \u0004 noted.
- Models: primary inference on Llama2-chat 13B quantized (default), occasional fallbacks to 70B for long-form assist (~20% of traffic).
- Traffic profile (estimated):
  - Steady-state requests: ~30 reqs/sec
  - Peak burst: up to 120 reqs/sec during business hours (concurrent active sessions ~100-120)
  - Average prompt + response: ~500 tokens (input 200 / output 300)
  - Token mix: ~80% short interactions (<=200 tokens), ~20% long (<=1500 tokens)
- SLOs: P95 latency target for 13B model <300ms; occasional 70B requests can be higher but should remain <2s.

Ask: can you confirm the burst concurrency (100 vs 120) and whether the 70B fallbacks are synchronous or can be queued/batched (i.e., can we accept slightly higher latency for those)? That affects whether we recommend A10G-heavy fleet (cost-optimized) vs A100/H100 nodes.

I've attached a quick sizing workbook (nova_health_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the assumptions above. Rafael will follow up with a preliminary node recommendation and rough pricing.

Next steps:
- Luke: confirm concurrency/batching expectations and procurement timeline
- Rafael/Aditya: provide 2 sizing options (cost-optimized and performance-optimized) by end of week
- Marissa: sync on draft commercial terms and draft quote

Thanks \u0004 talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type & TPS/Concurrency

Thanks Marissa - great write-up. Luke, a few quick notes from the sizing side and a first-pass recommendation: 

Assumptions (based on Marissa's notes):
- Avg tokens/request: 500 tokens
- Steady RPS: 30 req/s -> 15k tokens/s
- Peak RPS: 120 req/s -> 60k tokens/s
- Model mix: 80% 13B quantized, 20% 70B (higher memory/compute)

Rough capacity math (very high level):
- Llama2-13B quantized on A10G: ~3.5k tokens/s per GPU (in our runtime with batching/kv cache) -> need ~5-6 A10G for steady, ~18 A10G for peak.
- Llama2-13B quant on A100-80GB: ~9-10k tokens/s per GPU -> need ~2 A100 for steady, ~6 A100 for peak.
- 70B falls back to A100/H100 and is much heavier (estimate ~2-3x the per-token cost). If 20% of requests hit 70B synchronously, plan +25-30% headroom.

Recommendations (two options):
1) Cost-optimized: 12x A10G nodes with autoscaling/burst pool to handle spikes (falls back to queued longer-form). Good if NovaHealth can accept slightly longer tails on 70B.
2) Performance-optimized: 4x A100-80GB nodes (primary) + 2x A10G for low-cost routing. This keeps p95 latency for 13B <300ms and handles 70B fallbacks with better headroom.

I'll attach the sizing workbook with the per-GPU throughput rows and a rough cost model. Also flagged items that affect sizing: quantization format, KV cache hit rate, and allowed batching latency.

Attachment: [attachment: nova_health_sizing_v1.xlsx]

Happy to jump on a quick follow if you want to walk numbers.

-Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rafael - thanks for the quick follow. A couple clarifications from our infra side: 

- Concurrency: we expect sustained concurrency around 80-100, with short 15-30 minute bursts up to ~140 when several clinics start sessions simultaneously. Please size for 120 as a conservative baseline.
- 70B usage: currently synchronous for advanced QA flows and transcript summarization (approx 15-20% of queries). Latency sensitivity: those requests can tolerate up to ~3s but we prefer sub-2s if possible.
- Security: NovaHealth requires private peering into our VPC and SOC2 evidence (we'll send the questionnaire). If Dedicated can be provisioned inside our VPC (private deployment), that is preferred, but we can evaluate Dedicated with private peering.
- Procurement: aiming to finalize PO in 6-8 weeks; approval chain is starting next week.

I'll attach the SOC2 contact and our procurement timeline separately.

Thanks - Luke
